biography.plain_text: Robert C. Roebling was an American heir and cattle breeder who settled on Skidaway Island, near Savannah, with his wife, Dorothy. His family wealth came from wire manufacturing, and he received an inheritance through his father's estate. The couple donated their Modena property to Georgia for the Skidaway Institute of Oceanography.

confidence.reason: Primary court inheritance, university family history and donation records support the concise identity.

biography.html: Robert C. Roebling was an American heir and cattle breeder who settled on Skidaway Island, near Savannah, with his wife, Dorothy. long_biography.plain_text:
Robert C. Roebling developed Modena Plantation as a breeding farm for Angus cattle. He hired animal-husbandry graduate George Gibson to manage the herd after hearing how Gibson had transported a bull across Georgia. Breeding stock included a close relative of an international champion, and cattle sold from the island had to be ferried to the mainland.

Roebling also worked with John C. Reuter to establish a sports-car circuit near Savannah. He raised money for the project while Reuter organised its construction. The track served racing drivers, local school pupils and the Georgia State Patrol, combining competition with driving instruction.
